text:
For the equilibrium,  

$2H_{2}O$ $⇌$  $H_{3}O^{+} + OH^{-}$, the value of $\DeltaG^{o}$ at 298 K is approximately :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $2~\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}+\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$, the activity of pure water is 1, so at 298 K

$K=[\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}][\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}]=K_{w}=1.0\times 10^{-14}$

$\Delta G^{\circ }=-2.303RT\log K=-2.303\times 8.314\times 298\times \log \left (10^{-14}\right )$

$\Delta G^{\circ }=5705.8\times 14\text{J mol}^{-1}\approx 7.99\times 10^{4}\text{J mol}^{-1}\approx 80\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

The large positive value matches the very small extent of self-ionisation of water.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text: The reaction, MgO(s) + C(s) $\to$ Mg(s) + CO(g), for which $\Delta_{r}H^{o} = 491.1 kJ$ mol$^{–1}$ and $\Delta_{r}S^{o} = 198.0 JK^{–1}$  mol$^{–1}$, is not feasible at 298 K. Temperature above which reaction will be feasible is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$\DeltaG^{o} =$ $\DeltaH^{o} - T\DeltaS^{o}$

For a reaction to be spontaneous $\DeltaG^{o}$ must be negative i.e.,

T$\DeltaS^{o} >$ $\DeltaH^{o}$

$\Rightarrow$ T > $\frac{\Delta H^{\circ }}{\Delta S^{\circ }}$

$\Rightarrow$ T > $\frac{491.1\times 1000}{198}$

$\Rightarrow$ T > 2480.3 K
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text: The de Broglie wavelength ($λ$) associated with a photoelectron varies with the frequency (v) of the incident radiation as, [$v_{0}$ is threshold frequency] :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By photoelectric effect

KE = h$ν$ - h$ν_{o}$ ....(1)

de broglie wavelength,

$λ$ = $\frac{h}{mv}$ = $\frac{h}{\sqrt{2m\times K.E}}$ ...(2)

Using equation (1) and (2), we get

$λ$ = $\frac{h}{\sqrt{2m\times (hν-hν_{0})}}$

$\therefore$ $λ\propto \frac{1}{(v-v_{0})^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text: 25 ml of the given HCl solution requires 30 mL of 0.1 M sodium carbonate solution. What is the volume of this HCl solution required to titrate 30 mL of 0.2 M aqueous NaOH solutions ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Standardisation: $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}+2\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$, so 1 mol of $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}$ reacts with 2 mol of HCl.

Moles of $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}=0.1\times 30=3$ mmol, so HCl present in 25 mL $=2\times 3=6$ mmol.

$M_{\mathrm{HCl}}=\dfrac{6\text{mmol}}{25\text{mL}}=0.24\text{M}$

With NaOH: $\mathrm{HCl}+\mathrm{NaOH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ (1 : 1). Moles of NaOH $=0.2\times 30=6$ mmol.

$V_{\mathrm{HCl}}=\dfrac{6\text{mmol}}{0.24\text{M}}=25\text{mL}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text:
The reaction 2X $\to$ B is a zeroth order reaction. If the initial concentration of X is 0.2 M, the half-life is 6 h. When the initial concentration of X is 0.5 M, the time required to reach its final concentration of 0.2 M will
be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For zero order reaction,

$t_{1/2} =$ $\frac{a_{0}}{2k}$

$\Rightarrow$ k = $\frac{a_{0}}{2t_{1/2}}$ = $\frac{0.2}{2\times 6}$ = 1.67 $\times$ $10^{-2}$ mol $L^{–1}h^{–1}$

For zero order reaction,

$A_{0} - A_{t} = kt$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.5 - 0.2 = 1.67 $\times$ $10^{-2} t$

$\Rightarrow$ t = $\frac{0.3}{1.67\times 10^{-2}}$ = 18 h
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text:
Given the equilibrium constant: 

$K_{C}$ of the reaction : 

$Cu(s) + 2Ag^{+} (aq)$ $\to$ $Cu^{2+} (aq) + 2Ag(s)$ is 

10 $\times$ $10^{15}$,  calculate the E${}_{cell}^{0}$ of this reaction at 298 K 

[2.303 $\frac{RT}{F}$  at  298 K = 0.059V]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$\DeltaG^{o} = -$RTln$(K_{C}) ....(1)$

Also $\DeltaG^{o} = -nFE_{cell}^{o}$ ....(2)

$\therefore$ -nF$E_{cell}^{o}$ = -RTln$(K_{C})$

$\Rightarrow$ $E_{cell}^{o}$ = $\frac{RT}{nF}\ln (K_{C})$

= $2.303\frac{RT}{nF}\log (K_{C})$

= $\frac{0.059}{2}\log \left (10\times 10^{15}\right )$

( n = no of electron transferred = 2 )

= 0.059 $\times$ $\frac{16}{2}$

= 0.059 $\times$ 8

= 0.472 V
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text: The number of bridging CO ligand(s) and Co-Co bond(s) in $Co_{2}(CO)_{8}$, respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the solid state, $\mathrm{Co}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{8}$ has two Co atoms joined by one Co–Co bond and bridged by two CO groups; each Co also carries three terminal CO groups ($2+3+3=8$ CO).


[IMG]

Each Co has 9 valence electrons and gains 6 from its three terminal CO, 1 from each of the two bridging CO and 1 from the Co–Co bond: $9+6+2+1=18$.

So $\mathrm{Co}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{8}$ has 2 bridging CO ligands and 1 Co–Co bond.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text: Which of the following compounds reacts with ethylmagnesium bromide and also decolourizes bromine water solution:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A compound reacts with $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{MgBr}$ if it has an acidic hydrogen or an electrophilic group such as $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$, $-\mathrm{COOR}$ or $-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$; it decolourises bromine water if it has a reactive C=C.

(A), 2-methoxystyrene: the vinyl group decolourises bromine water, but an aryl methyl ether has no acidic hydrogen and no electrophilic group, so it does not react with $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{MgBr}$.

(B): $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{MgBr}$ adds to the $-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$ group and attacks the ester $-\mathrm{COOCH}{}_{3}$, and the conjugated diene in the ring adds bromine (1,2- or 1,4-addition), decolourising bromine water.

(C), 2-vinylphenol: the phenolic OH protonates $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{MgBr}$, releasing ethane, and the vinyl group decolourises bromine water.

(D): the ketone and the nitrile react with $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{MgBr}$, but there is no C=C outside the benzene ring, so bromine water is not decolourised.

Hence, the correct options are (B) and (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text:
In the following compound,  


[IMG]


the favourable site/s for protonation is/are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At (a) position lone pair of N atom is in resonance with $π$ bond so lone pair can't donate easily to $H^{+}$ ion.

At (b) position N atom is directly connected with double bond so lone pair of N atom doesn't participate in resonance so lone pair can be donated easily to $H^{+}$ ion.

At (c) position N atom is directly connected with double bond so lone pair of N atom doesn't participate in resonance so lone pair can be donated easily to $H^{+}$ ion.

At (d) position N atom is directly connected with double bond so lone pair of N atom doesn't participate in resonance so lone pair can be donated easily to $H^{+}$ ion.

At (e) position lone pair of N atom is in resonance with $π$ bond so lone pair can't donate easily to $H^{+}$ ion.

$\therefore$ (b), (c) and (d)  are the favourable sites for protonation.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot
